newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end off, dragged down by mining sector.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end off, dragged down by mining sector.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed lower Wednesday as investors fretted over the stability of lofty zinc prices and sold mining stocks, brokers said.
But brewery and construction stocks resisted the undertow as players believed these sectors would gain along with the overall economy this year, they added.
The sectoral factors were seen dominating the market Thursday, they said.
Wednesday, the General Index fell 0.47 percent to 2,092.7 points, according to preliminary figures.
The blue-chip Selective Index dropped 0.72 percent to 2,990.2 points. In a total of 1,812 trades, volume was a low 26.0 million soles ($9.8 million).
"The market was apathetic. There were large fluctuations -- especially in the mining stocks because of the zinc price," Jorge Gutirrez of local brokerage Coril said.

Atacocha fell 1.77 percent to close at 2.78 soles on volume of 280,000 shares, despite reporting a net profit for the first half of 7.0 million soles, compared to a 3.3 million sol loss in the same period last year.
Benchmark Telefnica del Per ended down 1.09 percent at 6.35 soles on volume of 502,000 shares.
The country's leading brewery UCP Backus climbed 1.29 percent to 2.35 soles on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Peru's top cement company, Cementos Lima, closed up 2.50 percent at 5.73 soles on volume of 112,000 shares.
